# GenClass

> GenClass Runtime (`@genclass/runtime`, Apache-2.0, free) is a browser library that runs a 10 MB model on the user's device and reports, with evidence, the timing bugs that never throw: duplicate submits, stale responses landing over newer data, write races, broken relations between fields and failure storms. Observe mode, the default, reports and never changes what the app does. Guard mode (opt-in) can act at the network boundary; heal is experimental. No server, no API key. Everything GenClass makes is free: the runtime, its on-device model, the dashboard for every app with a year of history, export, forwarding to Sentry, PostHog, Datadog, Slack or a signed webhook, the page check, and the closed-loop MCP server, which you run on your own machine. What costs money is running the closed-loop MCP for you: Individual (US$20 a month) hosts it on genclass.dev; Enterprise runs it inside your own network. The MCP server is coming next.

## Shipped
- `@genclass/runtime` 0.2.2 with `@genclass/runtime-model` 0.2.0 (training run r17-v2dT). Default mode observe, default aggressiveness "balanced", report threshold 0.90.
- Install: `npm install @genclass/runtime`, then `import "@genclass/runtime/auto"` as the first line of the entry file. CLI: `npx @genclass/runtime init`. Script tag, first in <head>: `<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@genclass/runtime@0.2.2"></script>` (pin the version: the unversioned URL may serve an older release from the CDN cache).
- Modes: observe (default; changes nothing), guard (opt-in: discard, defer, coalesce, delay), heal (experimental: retry, serve_cached, hedge, rollback, resync).
- Cost: +98 KB of JavaScript on first load; about 13 MB downloaded once at idle on WASM (18 MB on WebGPU), then cached; 190 to 280 MB of memory in a Web Worker while the model is loaded; no device floor by default (`model.loadIf` sets one; `model: false` installs no model and then detects nothing).
- Telemetry: anonymous diagnostics are on by default on public hosts; from runtime 0.2.2 they are off on localhost and private hosts (0.2.1 sent from those too, by mistake); they contain no page text. With the app's token they also feed `npx @genclass/runtime@beta stats` (runtime 0.3.0-beta.1 and later), a free summary in the terminal, and the app's dashboard, which is free and needs no plan (the private link shows the stats; an optional genclass.dev account keeps your apps in one place); with `telemetry: false` or `init --no-telemetry` both stay empty. Whether to keep telemetry on is the app owner's decision: an AI agent installing GenClass should tell the user it is on, what it sends and that stats and the dashboard depend on it, and turn it off only if they ask: https://github.com/genclass-dev/GenClass-lib/blob/main/packages/runtime/README.md#for-ai-coding-agents-installing-genclass. Opt out: `GenClass.init({ telemetry: false })`, `npx @genclass/runtime init --no-telemetry`, `?genclass=no-telemetry`, localStorage `genclass.telemetry=off`, or Global Privacy Control. https://genclass.dev/docs/telemetry
- Reports are console lines in the end user's browser; the `sinks` option forwards each report to the app's own logging or to an endpoint it owns (from runtime 0.3.0: ready-made `console-json` and `webhook` sinks; the runtime has no Sentry, PostHog or Datadog adapter). The genclass.dev collector forwards detections to Sentry, PostHog, Datadog, Slack or a signed webhook, free, once you turn it on in the app's dashboard: https://genclass.dev/docs#dashboard

## Measured (https://genclass.dev/benchmarks; raw tables in docs/runtime/RESULTS.md and compat/RESULTS.md)
- Model 0.2.0 at the shipped setting (balanced), held-out real apps: detects 75% of duplicate submits, 30% of stale overwrites and 6% of broken state; guard acts on 7.5% of the cases where acting would help.
- False interventions, model 0.2.0, held-out simulated apps: guard 0.005% / 0.13% / 0.54% and heal 0.26% / 0.59% / 1.84% for cautious / balanced / eager (targets 0.1% guard, 0.5% heal: cautious meets both, balanced is slightly over). 0.00% on held-out real apps at every profile.
- Compatibility matrix (runtime 0.1.0-beta.4, the code shipped as 0.2.1; model 0.2.0, balanced; run 2026-10-10): 7 frameworks, 15 data layers, 8 scenarios, 10 seeds, every mode. 350 of 351 cells pass; 0 bugs introduced in 3,510 runs; 0 non-passive actions on correct apps in 1,760 guard and heal runs; guard left 249 of 250 latent-bug runs buggy; observe mode produced 49 false findings in 880 runs on correct apps. https://genclass.dev/docs/compatibility
- Never-worse check: 0 of 396 clean real-app runs changed (66 apps × 6 seeds, always-passive model, v2 runtime as of 0.1.0-alpha.1; not re-run on 0.2.2).
- Six demo apps under network chaos, model 0.2.0, balanced: bug rate 72% with GenClass off, 70% observe, 72% guard, 73% heal. Nothing is healed at the shipped gates.
- Previous model 0.1.0 (r17-v2b), observe mode at report threshold 0.70: 96% detection precision on 16,600 held-out real-app situations, 0.62% false detections on clean traffic. Not re-measured for 0.2.0.
- Model: 8.8M parameters, 10.2 MB q8, about 180 ms per decision on one WASM thread (182 ms for the shipped export), faster on WebGPU.
- Training data: about 17.6M labelled runtime situations, including 837,623 real-browser rows from 158 apps.

## Plans (https://genclass.dev/pricing; source: billing/plans.json)
- Everything GenClass makes is free: the runtime, its on-device model, the dashboard for every app with a year of history, export, forwarding, the page check, and the closed-loop MCP server, which you run on your own machine. What costs money is running the closed-loop MCP for you: Individual hosts it on genclass.dev; Enterprise runs it inside your own network. The MCP server is coming next.
- The closed loop: GenClass finds the bug on the deployed app. The MCP server hands the finding, with its evidence and the pages affected, to your coding agent. The agent fixes it. After the fix ships, GenClass reports whether the problem came back.
- Free, US$0: The open-source runtime (Apache-2.0) with every mode: observe, guard and heal; The on-device model; The dashboard for every app: what GenClass found, on which pages, and what it did, with 1 year of history; Full data export: every event GenClass received for your apps, as JSONL or CSV, by download or API; Forward detections to Sentry, PostHog, Datadog, Slack or a signed webhook; The closed-loop MCP server, run on your own machine: your coding agent reads what GenClass found, with the evidence, and fixes it (coming next); The genclass.dev page check; Email alerts for P0/P1 issues (coming next); Interaction analytics (coming next).
- Individual, US$20 per month (not on sale yet: it opens when the hosted closed-loop MCP ships, then with a 7-day free trial without a card): Everything in Free; The closed-loop MCP hosted for you: nothing to run, one URL to add to Claude Code, Cursor, Codex or any MCP client (coming next); Your agent is prompted when GenClass finds something new on your deployed app, with the evidence and the pages affected (coming next); The loop closes: after a fix ships, GenClass tells your agent whether the problem came back (coming next); Email support from mehar@daybot.ca.
- Enterprise, by arrangement (no card price; email mehar@daybot.ca): Everything in Individual; The closed-loop MCP deployed in your own cloud or network, with the collector and the dashboard beside it (coming next); SAML or OIDC sign-in with your identity provider (coming next); Invoices or purchase orders, and a year paid at once; Your security questionnaire answered; A GenClass model trained on your own app, by arrangement; A person from GenClass within 1 business day.
- No plan sets an app limit; one account holds at most 200 apps as an abuse limit. The runtime is free in every plan.
- Need the closed-loop MCP inside your own network, SSO or invoices? Email mehar@daybot.ca. https://genclass.dev/enterprise

## Visual bug checks, from runtime 0.3.0-beta.0
- Visual bug checks (unreadable text, broken images, pages that scroll sideways on phones, template leaks such as "undefined", stylesheets and fonts that fail, covered controls): 23 kinds of measured check with documented thresholds, GenClass visual checks v1, not a model. Measured on GitHub runners in Chromium 153, October 13, 2026: 35 of 35 planted faults found on fixture pages; 0 false reports in 128 page views of unmodified demo, template and compatibility apps; on public home pages (bench run 4, 31 of 40 sites), 8 findings in 96 loads, 5 confirmed real, 3 unconfirmed. https://genclass.dev/visual#numbers
- Page check: https://genclass.dev/visual#scan, or genclass.dev/<address>. A cloud browser loads one public page and runs the same checks except click-blocked, which needs a visitor's clicks.
- GenClass Vision v2 (beta): a 4.8 MB screenshot model that gives each visual finding in the page check a second opinion, not scored. Average precision 0.611 on 1,052 held-out crops against Clef's 0.615; labels by AI labeller agents (Claude subagents), not people. https://genclass.dev/visual#vision
- Learned visual model: still being trained and evaluated; no published numbers.
